title: CJ Rosser commits to North Carolina: Five-star forward is the next big recruiting win for Michael Malone - CBS Sports

body:
Rosser is the No. 2-ranked prospect in the 2027 class. North Carolina now has two of the top-five recruits for this cycle
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Five-star forward CJ Rosser committed to North Carolina on Tuesday, giving first-year coach Michael Malone another massive win on the recruiting trail. Rosser, who is the No. 2-ranked player in the 2027 recruiting cycle by 247Sports, joins a UNC recruiting class that already features five-star wing DeMarcus Henry, the No. 4 player in the class.UNC is the lone team with two top-10 commitments in the 2027 recruiting cycle. In fact, UNC has never landed two top-10 ranked high school players from the same recruiting class in the 247Sports era. Rosser is set to join Henry, Harrison Barnes and Cole Anthony as the highest-ranked recruits in UNC basketball history.The Southeastern Prep product (Orlando, FL) committed to UNC over Arkansas, Kentucky, Miami, and NC State.Last month, Henry became UNC's first member of its 2027 recruiting class when the five-star wing committed to UNC over Louisville, Arkansas and Kentucky. Rosser joins Cayden Daughtry (Arkansas) as the highest-ranked players from the 2027 recruiting class to announce their respective pledges for next season.
247Sports Director of Scouting Adam Finklestein notes that Rosser's tools are "undeniable""Ultimately, his natural talent, and two-way tools, are undeniable, so while he may have a long way to go before the consistency of his production lives up to the totality of his potential, some of that has proven to be contextual. Additionally, while the conversation is often about his upside, the overlap of those sheer tools also gives him a deceptively high floor."The last month has been busy with several of the biggest names in the 2027 recruiting class coming off the board. Henry joins Lewis Uvwo (Providence), Reese Alston (LSU), Asa Montgomery (Duke), Henry (North Carolina) and Daughtry (Arkansas) as players from the class who announced where they will be playing college basketball next season.
Notably, Beckham Black, the No. 1-ranked player in the 2027 recruiting class, has yet to announce where he will be playing next season.

title: College football coaching carousel 2026: Tracking all the changes so far - CBS Sports
description: Get the latest on the college football coaching carousel as CBS Sports tracks new hires and fires
body:
Get the latest on the college football coaching carousel as CBS Sports tracks new hires and fires
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After a few false starts, the coaching carousel finally started spinning in late October. It's not surprising the silly season is off to a slow start after 2025's record-breaking churn. The FBS hired 32 new head coaches, including 17 in the four power conferences, and hundreds more assistant coaches changed jobs. Ninety-three FBS programs have changed coaches over the last three offseasons. The question is whether we've hit a cooling period as schools wrestle with the challenging economics of the NIL and revenue-sharing era.  Maryland kicked off the firing season Oct. 21. More power programs have followed. CBS Sports is tracking every move in the 2026-27 cycle and grading each hire below. 
 Power Four 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Baylor — OUT: Dave Aranda | IN: TBD Dave Aranda won a Big 12 title in 2021 but otherwise led the Bears with middling success over seven seasons. He finished 40-40 and was below .500 in the Big 12 (26-32). Don't be surprised if Baylor seeks an offensive coach, particularly one with strong connections to the Texas high school scene. UTSA's Jeff Traylor, Texas State's GJ Kinne and USC's Lincoln Riley are strong candidates to consider in Waco. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Florida State — OUT: Mike Norvell | IN: Glenn SchumannFlorida State shook the Nick Saban tree and snagged Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann as its next coach. Schuman spent the last 10 seasons alongside Kirby Smart at Georgia, where he was co-defensive coordinator from 2019-23 before he was elevated to DC in 2024. His defenses have improved in each of the last two seasons, and he enters the final week of the regular season allowing less than 14 points per game. Florida State cut ties with Mike Norvell on Nov. 1 following a loss to Clemson.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Maryland — OUT: Mike Locksley | IN: TBD Maryland kicked off the coaching carousel this year. Mike Locksley is out halfway through his eighth season at Maryland, where he was 39-54 overall. The Terps were 4-8 in back-to-back seasons leading to the decisive 2026. A wide variety of candidates will be considered in College Park. Wake Forest's Jake Dickert, a popular name elsewhere, and Memphis' Charles Huff, a Maryland native, immediately come to mind. Dickert, however, recently signed a new contract with Wake. The Terps have better NIL resources than a year ago, but the job is still difficult in the Big Ten. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    NC State — OUT: Dave Doeren | IN: Philip Rivers NC State legend Philip Rivers was hired to lead his former program to the mountaintop of the ACC. The legendary NFL quarterback spent six years coaching St. Michael's Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama, where he led the program to the playoffs four times. His son, Gunner, is a quarterback committed to NC State. With only a $3.5 million annual salary, NC State is counting on fans and boosters to help fund NIL and secure an elite roster.  Dave Doeren was fired during his 14th season in Raleigh, following a disappointing 31-28 loss at Stanford that dropped the Wolfpack to 1-3 in the ACC. Doeren seemed just good enough to win seven to nine games every year, but disappointing losses always railroaded what could have been special seasons. A downtick in success over the last three years made it clear a change was needed. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    TCU — OUT: Sonny Dykes | IN: TBDFour years after leading TCU to the national championship game, Sonny Dykes is out in Fort Worth. The Horned Frogs simply weren't able to sustain that success, though they did string together nine consecutive wins in 2024 and 2025. In 2026, however, TCU has regressed noticeably with a 5-6 record through 11 games. The Horned Frogs are fielding the 103rd scoring offense in the country, and that side of the ball is supposed to be Dykes' bread and butter.
MORE FROM 247 SPORTS: Live updates on the 2027 coaching carousel Group of Six 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    UTEP — OUT: Scotty Walden | IN: TBD Scotty Walden is out after a 1-9 start in his third season leading UTEP. His tenure produced only six wins across three seasons and the nation's worst-scoring offense in 2026. The Miners' athletics program is among the worst-funded in the country, making this job incredibly challenging. Remember, Walden was coaching at FCS Austin Peay before coming to El Paso, so the list of candidates this time around could be shallow. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Sam Houston — OUT: Phil Longo | IN: TBD Phil Longo didn't last long at Sam Houston. He was fired during his second season after the Bearcats started 1-7. He was only 3-17 with a 1-11 record in Conference USA. The program is not far removed from transitioning from the FCS to the FBS, but it's also only been two years since former coach K.C. Keeler led the Bearcats to a 10-3 record with a win in the New Orleans Bowl. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Arkansas State — OUT: Butch Jones | IN: TBD Butch Jones is out after a 4-6 start to his sixth season at Arkansas State, where he was 30-43 overall. The Red Wolves are aching for a return to their success in the 2010s, when the program rotated through future Power Four coaches Hugh Freeze, Gus Malzahn and Bryan Harsin while recording nine straight winning seasons.

body:
A reunion with Jayden Daniels, an NFC West revenge tour and two potential AFC opportunities headline Aiyuk's most intriguing options
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Brandon Aiyuk is up for grabs after the San Francisco 49ers released Aiyuk on Monday, ending the duo's tumultuous relationship. The NFL granted San Francisco a two-week roster spot exemption when the league reinstated him on Nov. 9, but with that exemption ending on Monday, the 49ers moved on. Aiyuk hasn't played in a game since his 2024 torn ACL and MCL, which means he never played a snap on his four-year, $120 million extension he signed right before the start of that season. That contract possesses a $40.5 million cap hit for 2027, so any team that wishes to acquire him will likely allow him to clear waivers first before signing him. The last full season Aiyuk played, San Francisco won the NFC and lost to the Kansas City Chiefs in overtime of the Super Bowl, with him playing like one of the league's best pass catchers. Brandon Aiyuk, 2023 seasonNFL rankReceiving yards1,3427th100-yard receiving games7T-4thYards per reception17.92ndRate of catches for a first down or a touchdown81.3%1stYards per route run3.12nd* The 2023 season was Aiyuk's last fully healthy season played So which teams could be interested in the 28-year-old's services? 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Washington CommandersThe Washington Commanders are the obvious landing spot. He has previously openly campaigned to join because of his connection with Jayden Daniels. They played together at Arizona State in 2019, Aiyuk's senior year and Daniels' freshman year, and Aiyuk racked up 1,192 yards receiving and eight touchdowns on 65 catches during their 12 games together. 
Washington also has a glaring need at wide receiver. Terry McLaurin went down with a torn patellar tendon in his left knee, and veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs, who is on a one-year contract, is the only player with more than two receiving touchdowns, six, on the Commanders this season. Aiyuk might behave himself for Daniels in Washington. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Pittsburgh SteelersThe Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4) are clinging to the AFC's No. 7 seed, the third and final wildcard spot, after consecutive losses. They face-planted against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10 and the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11. Pittsburgh needs more offensive firepower ASAP. Aaron Rodgers would likely welcome all the help he can get, especially after hot-headed wide receiver DK Metcalf got himself ejected on Sunday. Metcalf and Aiyuk would be a handful, but Rodgers is one of the few quarterbacks who has the skins on the wall to get them in check. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Los Angeles RamsIf Aiyuk really wanted to stick it to the 49ers, joining the NFC West rival Los Angeles Rams would be one way to do it. The Rams are on the cusp of the NFC's No. 7 seed, but it will be a slog for them to actually reach the playoffs without their best two wide receivers available. Puka Nacua is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season after undergoing surgery for an MCL injury in his knee. Davante Adams, who led the league with 14 receiving touchdowns in 2025, is still sidelined with a hamstring injury that could have him out for a few more weeks. That means quarterback Matthew Stafford, who has only been around league average this season with the No. 15 passer rating (92.8) and No. 13 expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.08), needs to rediscover his 2025 NFL MVP form ASAP. Having Aiyuk could help expedite that process.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    New England PatriotsThere's a chance Drake Maye doesn't return to action this season because of the fibula injury he suffered in Week 10 against the Detroit Lions. However, the Patriots (5-5) are just a game out of the AFC playoff picture. Blockbuster trade acquisition A.J. Brown has been a bust so far, and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) is on injured reserve. If Mike Vrabel wants to do everything he can to make sure the defending AFC champs don't miss out on the 2026 postseason, signing Aiyuk could make some sense.

title: NBA trade rumors: Lakers planning to be active, Jazz looking elsewhere after Kyrie Irving buzz - CBS Sports
description: NBA trade season is still weeks away, but buzz is building one month into the 2026-27 season
body:
NBA trade season is still weeks away, but buzz is building one month into the 2026-27 season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:16 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        We're now a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while we're still weeks away from the unofficial start of trade season (Dec. 15), we've seen enough basketball for teams to at least begin making plans for the upcoming transaction cycle. Teams are starting to know how good they are, what sort of holes they're dealing with and what the market is going to look like as we draw closer to the February trade deadline.Firm rumors are still in short supply, but we're at least getting some early buzz on who plans to do what in the months to come. So let's check in on what has made the rounds lately.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Lakers plan to be active at deadlineThe 14-3 Los Angeles Lakers are headed for a titanic clash with the San Antonio Spurs on Friday that will presumably put one of those two teams in pole position in the Western Conference. Last Friday, however, head of basketball operations Rob Pelinka did a pregame interview with Spectrum SportsNet in which he made it clear he plans to be aggressive ahead of February's deadline."We'll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see," Pelinka said. "We think this team has a real chance to make a run, so we want to give the group as much talent as we can. Don't want to get too far over our skis with a hot start, because you don't want to get big-headed, but clearly the way it's gone so far, it's been great and we hope it continues."
The Lakers are very limited in terms of tradable draft capital because of their big July swing for Walker Kessler. They only have one first-round asset available, and it's only swap rights in 2032. They picked up two useful second-round picks in the Deandre Ayton trade, though, giving them three in total. That's not enough for a blockbuster, but it's helpful liquidity. Further, the Lakers are relatively financially flexible going into the deadline as well. They're barely over the luxury-tax line and have around $8 million in room beneath their first apron hard cap, allowing them to potentially make a somewhat unbalanced trade if the need presents itself.So, what would the Lakers be looking for at the deadline? Two obvious needs stand out:Backup center. The Lakers are almost 12 points per 100 possessions worse without Walker Kessler on the floor, and given Kessler's past durability issues, they have to be better-prepared for games he misses outright.Wing depth. The Lakers did extremely well with minimal resources on the wing over the summer, getting Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams for the minimum. Both have outplayed those contracts significantly, but their shooting will be tested in the playoffs, and either way, both are set to return to free agency next summer. Neither Williams nor Thybulle have ever played a typical starter's workload in the playoffs, and Jake LaRavia was a mess in last year's postseason. The Lakers won't have access to the sort of wings that typically win championships, but if they can cobble together a deep enough rotation of specialists, they might be good enough elsewhere to overcome that weakness.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Clippers gearing up to sellAs Marc Stein noted, the Los Angeles Clippers have moved to a veteran-only starting lineup, with Darius Garland, Rui Hachimura, Derrick Jones Jr., Max Strus and Brook Lopez opening games lately. Brandon Ingram, returning Monday, is sure to join that group, and Kris Dunn is a central part of their rotation. All of these players but Ingram and Garland are on expiring deals, and Stein noted that the Clippers are "regarded as a certain seller" ahead of the trade deadline.
And, well, that makes plenty of sense. The Clippers were just stripped of five first-round picks in the Kawhi Leonard scandal. Those expiring contracts belong to players who almost certainly won't be a part of the next great Clipper team, but they could help replenish the team's draft capital moving forward.The Clippers are, by far, the most versatile seller on the market right now. In theory, they could burnish just about any contender. Need defense? Jones and Dunn have you covered. Offense? Strus and Hachimura are proven playoff snipers. The center market is in the middle of a supply-demand crisis. Lopez has been sensational this season and could give any contender a solid 20 minutes per night. With Keaton Wagler in the building, it's hard to imagine they'd even shut the door on a good enough Garland offer. Expect the Clippers to live in the rumor mill for the next few months. They have several players who could legitimately impact the championship hunt.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jazz not so interested in Kyrie Irving after all?Last week, SNY dropped a stunner of a rumor: that the Utah Jazz, loaded with young guards and off to a terrible start, had had internal conversations about pursuing Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving. The rumor didn't make much sense in the moment, and The Salt Lake Tribune reported Monday that the Jazz "don't appear to have any real interest" in the future Hall of Famer. 
They have, however, talked trade with the team we just discussed: the Clippers. Those conversations began with "various Clippers bigs" and have moved on to wing depth, of which the Clippers have plenty. The Jazz are reportedly casting a wide net in pursuit of help.The 3-15 Jazz have been among the NBA's biggest disappointments this season. A lot of that has been the result of injuries, with Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen out now and Jusuf Nurkić having not yet debuted this season. The Jazz are painfully thin in the front court at this point, and the early partnership between Keyonte George and Darryn Peterson in the backcourt has yielded mixed results. Casting a wide net makes sense since the Jazz could theoretically use help basically anywhere. More of a playmaking guard to balance out the score-first instincts that George and Peterson bring would make sense. Wing depth, especially defense-first wing depth, would help address a major weakness. Dunn is a former Jazz player. And of course, adding some size to deal with all of those injuries would probably have the biggest immediate impact. Utah doesn't control its own first-round pick this year. The Jazz benefit from losing in no way, and that has seemingly made them eager to try to fight an uphill battle back into the Western Conference Play-In race.

title: Florida State hires Glenn Schumann: Seminoles tap Georgia defensive coordinator to replace Mike Norvell - CBS Sports
description: After a three-week coaching search, Florida State turns to Schumann to lead a Seminoles program seeking stability
body:
After a three-week coaching search, Florida State turns to Schumann to lead a Seminoles program seeking stability and progress
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:02 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Florida State hired Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann to be its next coach, the school announced Monday night. The Seminoles' search comes to an end just three weeks after firing previous coach Mike Norvell.This will be Schumman's first opportunity as a head coach, as he's spent his entire career as an assistant on the defensive side of the ball. Schumann began his career as a student assistant under Nick Saban at Alabama, and he worked his way up to director of football operations in 2014.When Kirby Smart left to take the Georgia vacancy in 2016, he brought Schumann along to be his inside linebackers coach. Schumann served in that role for three seasons until his promotion to co-defensive coordinator. In 2024, Schumann was promoted to the sole defensive coordinator role.Throughout his career at Georgia, Schumann has helped field some of the best defenses in college football. In 2021 and 2022 -- when the Bulldogs won consecutive national titles -- Schumann helped Smart engineer a pair of top-five scoring defenses.
With Schumann as the lone defensive coordinator, Georgia hasn't surrendered more than 20.6 points per game in a single season. In fact, the Bulldogs have only improved ever since then.YearPoints allowed/gameYards allowed/game202420.6329.9202517.6298.0202613.9267.0The Bulldogs have also developed a laundry list of NFL players under Smart and Schumann. Since the latter became co-defensive coordinator, Georgia has sent 35 defensive players to the NFL Draft.The obvious question about this hire is whether Schumann steps out of Smart's shadow and successfully runs his own program. There were the same questions about Smart when he left Saban's staff at Alabama, and that has worked out nicely for the Bulldogs. Florida State is hoping for a similar outcome.The Seminoles are hoping Schumann can reinvigorate a program that's been a step behind in the NIL and transfer portal era. Florida State is 12-23 over the last three seasons, and it's been a rudderless operation in Tallahassee.Now, Florida State will get a fresh start on a couple of levels. The man who hired Schumann, new FSU AD Jeff Purinton, was just hired on Nov. 9. Purinton has been tasked with leading the Seminoles' athletic department into the future -- as opposed to being mired in the old ways of doing business -- and he's tabbed Schumann as the man for the job on the football field."We are incredibly excited to announce Glenn Schumann as the next leader of our Florida State football program," Purinton said in a release. "I have known him since 2008 and have seen first-hand his growth as a coach. Glenn's abilities in all facets of the game, from organization to leadership to development and recruiting, are elite. He is a great person who will represent the Florida State program with class and integrity."Schumann gets his shotOver the last 18 years, Schumann has worked his way up the coaching ladder. During that time, he's worked under Saban and Smart, two of the best examples for an up-and-coming coach to follow.Of course, that doesn't guarantee success. The Saban and Smart coaching trees have produced their fair share of success stories. More recently, Georgia hit a home run when they plucked Smart from Alabama, and Dan Lanning has done very well for himself since leaving Georgia for Oregon.On the flip side, there have been some major disappointments, like Jim McElwain and Jeremy Pruitt. Neither of those coaches was able to stand on his own two feet away from legendary mentors.Now Schumann must prove that he's capable of leading an entire program -- and not just any program. Florida State is a major brand with a huge fan base. If Schumann gets off to an underwhelming start, the pressure will mount quickly. That's why it will be imperative for Schumann to show signs of progress in his debut season.Getting off to a good start will only be tougher with Schumann expected to remain with the Bulldogs for the remainder of the season. If Georgia makes a deep run in the College Football Playoff, as seems likely, Schumann will split his time between coaching in Athens and working the transfer portal in Tallahassee.Offensive coordinator hire is critical for FSUSchumann has spent the entirety of his career as an assistant on the defensive side of the ball. That's his specialty, and it's probably fair to assume the Florida State defense will be in good hands as long as Schumann is in town.
The bigger unknown is what Florida State's offense will look like under Schumann. Finding the right fit can sometimes be a challenge for defensive-minded coaches. Just look at what's happened at Oklahoma, where Brent Venables made a poor decision in hiring Ben Arbuckle. That hire showed signs of trouble in 2025 and completely derailed the 2026 season.On the more positive side, Schumann's current boss found a nice balance. Todd Monken was a tremendous success - resulting in two national championships - before he went to the NFL. Monken's replacement, Mike Bobo, is currently running the No. 3 scoring offense in the country.It will be interesting to see which direction Schumann goes on offense. Does he pull from existing relationships at Georgia, or does he look for someone more outside-the-box? Either way, he needs to get it right.

        The Arizona Cardinals have relieved Nick Rallis of his duties as defensive coordinator, according to multiple reports. Teryl Austin, a veteran coach who recently served as the Pittsburgh Steelers' defensive coordinator from 2022 to 2025, will serve as the interim defensive coordinator amid the vacancy.Rallis, 33, had served as the Cardinals' defensive coordinator since 2023, initially joining the team under former head coach Jonathan Gannon. Arizona retained Rallis after Gannon's dismissal at the end of the 2025 season, keeping him as defensive coordinator through new head coach Mike LaFleur's early tenure. Before Arizona, he spent two years as the Eagles' linebackers coach (where he won an NFC title in 2022) and three years as a Vikings defensive quality control coach. Arizona's defense has been one of the league's worst units this season. Through 11 weeks, the Cardinals' defense ranks 31st in the NFL in points allowed, 32nd in touchdown passes allowed, 24th in third-down efficiency, and 29th in red-zone efficiency. Despite being retained across two head coaches, the Cardinals defense never particularly excelled under Rallis. Arizona finished 31st, 24th, and 26th in defensive EPA per play between 2023 and 2025 under Gannon and Rallis; the Cardinals currently rank 31st through 11 weeks this season. Things had really begun to fall apart for Arizona in recent weeks. Cardinals' defense has allowed over 30 points in four of their last five games. They gave up 34 points in each of their last two games. During Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs, Arizona's defense allowed at least 435 total yards for a second straight game. The unit has forced just one turnover since Week 7, tied for the league's fewest over that span. 
The Cardinals are 3-8 this season in their first year under LaFleur. After winning its season opener, Arizona has had two losing streaks of at least three games. Sunday marked the Cardinals' third straight loss after their Week 8 upset win in Dallas. While the team's offense has been decimated with injury and roster turnover — starting four quarterbacks in four weeks, placing No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love on injured reserve, and losing their top three wide receivers to either trade or injury — the defense has remained relatively healthy over the course fo the year.

title: SEC schedules vote on possible LSU expulsion as RJ Luis dispute pushes league to the brink - CBS Sports
description: LSU's standoff with the SEC has escalated into a legal and political fight, with major penalties still in play
body:
LSU's standoff with the SEC has escalated into a legal and political fight, with major penalties still in play
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:33 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The ongoing battle between the SEC and LSU took another significant turn Monday when the conference announced in a legal filing that it will hold a meeting in early December to consider expelling the school from the league.The SEC's presidents and chancellors are scheduled to conduct a special meeting on Dec. 3, two days before the final SEC Championship Game in football, to "consider termination of LSU's membership to the SEC, regardless of whether LSU continues to play (RJ Luis)," per Monday's filing. It is the latest significant development in the standoff between LSU and the conference, which has included multiple lawsuits at both the state and federal levels over LSU trying to roster and play former professional players. It would take a two-thirds vote of qualifying members to purge LSU from the conference. While expulsion is still considered unlikely, multiple sources told CBS Sports there is enough frustration amongst the presidents and chancellors that at least some could be in favor of voting to expel LSU from the conference. The SEC's leaders approved a penalty structure this summer which includes a half-season suspension for a coach and a fine of up to 50% of a sport's annual budget, among other measures, for any program that violates the conference's policy on rostering former professional players. However, the SEC said in its legal filing it has "no avenue to penalize" LSU for its actions. 
That's because a Louisiana judge issued a preliminary injunction that included protecting LSU from punishment if it included Luis on the roster. The SEC stated it would abide by those terms and "not impose penalties or fines on LSU" for including Luis. Still, dating back to the football program's run-in with the SEC earlier this fall, sources have believed LSU would ultimately face repercussions for its actions. As one source told CBS Sports last week, "(LSU) may be begging for expulsion when over."
The latest drama has involved LSU's decision to play Luis, who previously played for St. John's, declared for the 2025 NBA Draft and signed two-way contracts with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics in 2025. While Luis never played in an NBA regular-season game, he did play in three preseason games. He was away from college basketball for more than a year before committing to Will Wade's LSU Tigers program this past May.Luis won a temporary restraining order to play for LSU in August. Despite that, the SEC claimed in a legal filing on Monday that LSU AD Verge Ausberry and Wade both told Sankey that Luis would not actually play for the Tigers. That stance seemed to change in mid-November when LSU informed the SEC that it would, in fact, roster Luis. 
Despite outrage throughout the SEC, which included discussions about potentially boycotting LSU games, according to CBS Sports' Matt Norlander, Wade played LSU against Louisiana-Monroe on Nov. 18. That further inflamed the situation and renewed discussions around the possibility of expelling LSU from the conference, according to sources. Multiple sources described the anger toward LSU as palpable and even worse than it was when LSU football coach Lane Kiffin briefly rostered multiple former professional football players. At the time, sources told CBS Sports in August that the votes to expel LSU were there if the institution wasn't willing to back down. LSU reversed course on Nov. 19 in a brief statement from LSU president Wade Rousse announcing that the Tigers would no longer play Luis. That decision came after a phone call between Rousse and Sankey, during which the severity of what would follow if LSU refused to heed the SEC's warnings became clear. The impetus for Monday's legal filing came from a call among SEC presidents last Thursday, after it became known that Rousse was standing down and ordering Wade to stop playing Ruis. On that call, per one source, the presidents decided to move forward with SEC legal counsel to seek a temporary restraining order and to proceed with further discussion of LSU's potential expulsion in December.
"It's not bluster," one SEC source said. "[The league] can't just ignore all of this and move on. ... And they don't want to be doing this every three months."The school and the league could reach an amicable resolution in the near future, but that will require LSU to provide tangible evidence and good-faith actions demonstrating that the school will abide by all league rules moving forward. As a few SEC sources have pointed out, Wade playing Luis last week escalated matters even beyond what Rousse, Wade and other LSU leaders could have anticipated. One likely mandate from the SEC will require concrete assurances from LSU that Louisiana governor Jeff Landry's influence over certain athletics matters will no longer determine how the university conducts itself under the SEC's bylaws.

        LSU star MiLaysia Fulwiley has rejoined the team and is cleared to play against Belmont on Monday after her felony charges were dropped, the school confirmed to CBS Sports. Fulwiley missed the Tigers' last two games after she was arrested on Nov. 14 for allegedly hitting a police officer with a vehicle. Fulwiley was booked on five counts, including aggravated assault and aggravated battery, both of which were felonies. The felony charges have since been dropped, East Baton Rouge District Attorney Hillar Moore told WAFB, but Fulwiley is still facing three misdemeanors for flight from an officer, resisting an officer and disobedience to an officer.The Louisiana State Police released a statement regarding the change in charges:"As with all arrests and investigations, the circumstances and evidence surrounding criminal charges are subject to review by the appropriate District Attorney's Office.After a thorough review with all involved parties, the charges were amended based on the circumstances and evidence presented.Louisiana State Police remains committed to ensuring that all incidents are thoroughly documented, evidence is carefully reviewed, and cases are handled in coordination with the appropriate prosecutorial authorities. This matter was handled in accordance with the same investigative standards and procedures applied to countless other cases."Fulwiley also released a statement regarding the incident:
"Saturday night ended in a situation that never should have happened, and my posts afterward made it worse. For that, I owe an apology to the officers involved and everyone who calls themselves a Tiger. I also want to apologize to my family and all those who love and support me. People see the purple and gold before they see me, and I want to carry myself in a way that's worthy of it, on the court and off."Rules and laws apply to everyone, including the instructions of officers working a game night in Baton Rouge. I respect the job those officers do, and I'll let the legal process run its course. My focus is doing what this program asks of me and earning back the trust of the people who count on me."Fulwiley transferred to LSU in 2025 after playing her first two collegiate seasons at South Carolina, where she won a national championship as a freshman. She is the reigning back-to-back SEC Sixth Player of the Year and is currently projected as a top 10 pick in the 2027 WNBA Draft. It's unclear how, or if, this incident will affect her standing with WNBA teams. Through her first four games this season, Fulwiley is averaging 17.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 4.3 assists, 4.3 steals and 2.8 blocks on 54.9% shooting. Her return will be a big boost to the Tigers as their schedule starts to ramp up following a very easy start to the season. LSU is 6-0 and ranked No. 9 in the country, but has played every game at home and hasn't faced an opponent in the top 100 in the Bart Torvik rankings. In fact, Belmont, which checks in at No. 135, will be the Tigers' toughest opponent yet. LSU's 109-point win over Texas Southern was the largest in Division I history, and the Tigers have won their first six games by an average of 71.3 points.

title: Washington Spirit part ways with Adrian Gonzalez after loss in NWSL Championship - CBS Sports
description: Gonzalez was at the helm for both Saturday's defeat to the Kansas City Current and the 2025 loss in the NWSL Cham
body:
Gonzalez was at the helm for both Saturday's defeat to the Kansas City Current and the 2025 loss in the NWSL Championship to Gotham FC
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 23, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:34 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Washington Spirit parted ways with head coach Adrian Gonzalez on Monday, less than 48 hours after a 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current that marked the team's third successive defeat in the NWSL Championship.Gonzalez was an assistant on the 2024 team that lost to the Orlando Pride in the final but he served as the interim before Jonatan Giraldez's midseason arrival from Barcelona. He then succeeded Giraldez after he left for France's OL Lyonnes, another club in Spirit owner Michele Kang's portfolio, midway through the 2025 campaign. He was a finalist for the NWSL's coach of the year award last season and maintained a consistency that has been a trademark for the Spirit in recent years, ensuring they continued to be serial contenders for titles under both Giraldez and Gonzalez.For all their ambition, though, the Spirit have struggled to win major titles in the years since Kang took over the club in 2022. Their only title since is the 2025 Challenge Cup, a one-off game against the Pride, and have failed to win the NWSL Shield despite inching close on a handful of occasions while also falling short in the NWSL Championship games. They also failed to win the Concacaf W Champions Cup earlier this year, losing 5-3 to Club America in the final."I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished together at the Washington Spirit and grateful to the players, staff, ownership and supporters for their commitment and support throughout my time here," Gonzalez said in a club statement. "It has been an honor to lead this group, and I'm especially proud of the resilience and character the team has shown. A special thank you to the Spirit fans, who make this club truly unique. The connection and bond we've built with you has meant so much to me and made my time here even more special. Your passion and support are something I will always remember. While this chapter comes to an end, I'm excited for what lies ahead for the club and wish everyone continued success."
Gonzalez's departure also comes after Haley Carter became the president of soccer operations in the build-up to the 2026 season. Carter was previously with the Orlando Pride, who won both the NWSL Shield and NWSL Championship in 2024 after years of being a bottom-dweller in the league."We are grateful to Adrian for his leadership and the success he has helped bring to the Spirit over the past three seasons," Carter said in a statement. "He has led the team with class and professionalism and made a lasting contribution to this club. As we plan for the Spirit's future, all parties believe a change in leadership is necessary to build on that success and achieve our long-term sporting goals."The search for Gonzalez's successor is underway and is likely to center around the Spirit's continuing quest to win the NWSL's top titles.
Spirit's title chase dictates coaching changeSince Kang's 2022 takeover, the ambitions of the Spirit have been clear as day. This is a team that is purpose-built to compete for titles, to the point that their attempts to keep Trinity Rodman in the NWSL led the league to create a brand-new rule and a historic contract for the player herself. The Spirit's entire roster, though, is impressive in its own right – Rodman counts Italy international Sofia Cantore amongst her partners in attack, while Tanzania's Clare Luvanga has scored four goals and notched three assists since her September arrival.Gonzalez understood the assignment, even if the only accolade he walked away with was the 2025 Challenge Cup. He actually leaves the Spirit with 32 wins from 58 and a 1.84 points-per-game record, the best tally from a coach in the history of the NWSL. The strike on his record is that the Spirit did not rise to the occasion in the championship both last year and especially on Saturday, when a physical Current disrupted the momentum of the game and rattled the Spirit from start to finish. His will be a tough act to follow, though – he was able to get the best out of the players despite the stop-start nature of his responsibilities in the early stretch of his tenure and only confirmed that the Spirit are a club with high standards.Considering the ambitions of the club, the coaching search will be an intriguing one. The Spirit are an attack-minded team and it would not be a surprise if a coach of that ilk lands the job, but Gonzalez's successor will ultimately be tasked with actually winning the titles that have eluded the club in recent years. Someone with a winning track record might be preferred and even if there are few obvious candidates, the Spirit likely have the pull – and the resources – to sign almost anyone they would like. It is not the only layer of uncertainty as the search begins – Carter has never hired a head coach during her years in NWSL front offices, joining the Pride after Seb Hines took the role and departing before his August departure.

title: MLB rumors: Mets' Tarik Skubal follow-up, where Blue Jays turn now, plus Yankees, Phillies, Red Sox, more - CBS Sports
description: Here are your offseason hot stove rumors on Monday, Nov. 23
body:
Here are your offseason hot stove rumors on Monday, Nov. 23

        The offseason's biggest domino fell late Sunday evening: Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets. It is far and away the richest pitching contract in history, crushing Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Dodgers. The Mets still have other things to address, including adding another starter, but they landed the winter's best free agent.It should be a busy week on the hot stove leading up to the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Monday's hot stove happenings.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Yankees sign Suter
The Yankees and left-hander Brent Suter have agreed to a one-year contract worth $4 million, reports the New York Post. Suter will make $3.75 million in 2026, and there's a $3.5 million club option for 2027 with a $250,000 buyout. He is the fourth reliever the Yankees have signed this offseason, joining David Bednar (accepted qualifying offer), Tim Hill, and Jonathan Loáisiga.With the bullpen mostly assembled, the Yankees figure to pivot to offense the rest of the offseason. They need a third base upgrade over Ryan McMahon and a right-handed hitting catcher to pair with the lefty-swinging Austin Wells. It seems likely the Yankees will go with Anthony Volpe at second base and Spencer Jones in center field, but those positions can be improved as well.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Mets add Goldschmidt
The Mets have agreed to a deal with free agent first baseman Paul Goldschmidt, reports the New York Post. It's a one-year deal worth $8 million, according to The Athletic. He will presumably pair with Jared Young in a first base platoon. We did not rank Goldschmidt, 39, among our top 50 free agents. He accepted a reduced role for the Yankees over the last two seasons and was a valuable clubhouse presence.At this point in his career, Goldschmidt is no longer an everyday player, but he remains a solid platoon bat. He hit .317/.402/.572 against lefties over the last two years, compared to .235/.271/.337 against righties. Goldschmidt can still play a nifty first base as well. The Mets received the worst first base production in the sport in 2027. Even late-career Goldschmidt should be an upgrade. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Blue Jays prioritizing Peralta
After missing out on Tarik Skubal, the Blue Jays are now believed to be prioritizing Freddy Peralta, according to MLB Network. Toronto has a very good one-two punch in Dylan Cease and José Soriano. Behind them are Spencer Arrighetti, Cody Ponce (returning from a torn ACL), Trey Yesavage, and maybe Jake Bloss and Ricky Tiedemann. There's room for another starter, for sure.
Peralta, Michael King, and Trevor Rogers are the best available free agent starters now that Skubal has signed. Rogers declined the qualifying offer and is attached to draft pick compensation, which perhaps makes King or Peralta more desirable. Any of the three would boost a Blue Jays rotation that has upside but not much in the way of reliability behind Cease and Soriano.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dodgers' rotation plansThe Dodgers are not expected to aggressively pursue pitching help after losing out on Tarik Skubal, reports The Athletic. They're comfortable letting things play out and seeing what shakes loose among second- and third-tier free agents. As much as the Dodgers would have liked to retain Skubal, they're in a spot where they didn't absolutely need him.Despite this year's biceps and knee injuries, Shohei Ohtani is expected to pitch next season. He'll join Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Blake Snell, and Yoshinobu Yamamoto in the rotation. Emmet Sheehan, Gavin Stone, and Justin Wrobleski are next in line, with prospects Jackson Ferris and Christian Zazueta not far away. The Dodgers could use another starter but aren't desperate for one. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Three teams interested in Duran
The Mariners, Padres, and Phillies are among the teams interested in Red Sox outfielder Jarred Duran, according to MassLive. The Red Sox tendered Duran a contract at Friday's deadline and will now look to trade him. The Jake Bauers signing pushed Duran, who had a .266 on-base percentage in 2026, out of the regular lineup. A trade is the logical next step.Philadelphia and San Diego badly need outfield help and are obvious fits for Duran. Even if the Mariners manage to re-sign Randy Arozarena, they could use another outfielder, though Duran would be a less-than-stellar fit for a lineup that is already heavily left-handed. Regardless, it seems unlikely Duran will be with the Red Sox by the time Opening Day arrives.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Favorites for SatoThe Blue Jays, Phillies, and Yankees are considered the favorites for Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports MLB.com. The Cubs and Mets are believed to have interest as well. Sato primarily played third base for the Hanshin Tigers but is not regarded as a strong defender, and it is likely that he will play first base or a corner outfield spot in MLB.
This past season, Sato, 28 in March, hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs and won Japan's Triple Crown. He is similar to Munetaka Murakami in that he has big left-handed power, swing-and-miss concerns, and defensive issues. Murakami is a much more patient hitter, however. Sato is an aggressive swinger and is unlikely to walk much or post a strong on-base percentage.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Details on offers for Skubal
The Blue Jays offered Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract in the $400 million range before he signed with the Mets, according to The Athletic. Meanwhile, the Dodgers never reached the point of making Skubal an offer, reports ESPN. Los Angeles was known to prefer a short-term, high-dollar contract to a long-term arrangement. Getting Skubal on such a deal always seemed unlikely. As for the Padres, they put forth an offer in the $400 million range but with deferrals that would have lowered the present day value, reports the New York Post. Skubal's contract with the Mets includes $30 million in deferred money, which will lower the present day value some, but not significantly. The exact deferrals in San Diego's offer are unknown.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Royals ink relieverThe Royals and left-handed reliever Caleb Theilbar are in agreement on a one-year deal, per ESPN. Theilbar, 39, was excellent for the Cubs in 2025, but took a step back in 2026, pitching to a 4.86 ERA (87 ERA+) and 1.30 WHIP with 60 strikeouts in 50 innings pitched. He did strand 18 of the 23 runners he inherited, which is an adequate clip for a middle-relief type. The Royals recently acquired late-inning lefty José Ferrer in a trade and Daniel Lynch remains in the bullpen, so Thielbar could well be their third option as a lefty in relief.
